newsitem.title: UK: UK shares firm at close, underpinned by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: UK shares firm at close, underpinned by Wall St.

text.p: ** UK's FTSE ends firm, supported by rally in Dow, T-bonds.
** Early surge to record high on FTSE fails to hold, dealers
say market awaits result of Thursday's election.
** Banks succumb to profit-taking though dealers say sector could
be squeezed higher short term; GKN up on U.S. aquisition.

With all hope of a return of the ruling Conservatives long since ruled out, dealers said the market should rally unless voters returned a "hung" parliament -- seen as ushering in a period of continuing political uncertainty.

"We didn't respond properly to Dow's rise overnight," said one dealer, "there is just a lack of interest ahead of tomorrow. But once we get the election out of the way, so long as Wall Street maintains its poise, we will see some relief and the market will test its highs again."

The Dow, which surged on Tuesday after weaker-than-expected economic reports, was up about 50 points as London closed --despite strong figures for first quarter growth which revived worries about that the Federal Reserve will tighten credit to ward off inflation pressures.
Some economists said 5.6 percent U.S. growth could be the year's peak.

After weeks of low trading volumes in UK equities during the lengthy election campaign, dealers said the result of poll could prompt some investment funds to push some of their above-average cash holdings into the market.
"There is so much cash around just waiting to come in," said the head equity trader at another brokerage, "the market is going to its all-time highs and beyond."
Gaining stocks in the FTSE 100 marginally outpaced decliners 49 to 48, in heavy volume of 886 million shares -- well above the depressed levels of recent weeks.
Dragon Oil was most active stock for a second day, unchanged at 4p in volume of 77 million amid bid speculation.
The FTSE 250 index of mid-range stocks closed 8.3 points lower at 4,498.7 and the Reuters-HSBC index of the top 150 UK shares was up 0.28 at 1,190.23.

Bank stocks were among the day's biggest decliners as some investors cashed in gains from the sector's recent strong run. Lloyds fell 11-1/2p to 563-1/2, Barclays lost 13p to 11.48-1/2 and NatWest dropped 20-1/2p to 730-1/2.

Analysts and dealers however said the sector could rise yet further short-term as investment funds upped their weighting in the sector ahead of the market debut of more demutualising building societies.
Engineer GKN was the day's biggest gainer in the FTSE 100, up 4.3 percent after a U.S. acquisition seen as boosting earnings in its first year.
Other recently out-of-favour industrial stocks also rose, led by Siebe -- up 14p at 911-1/2 as Kleinwort Benson repeated a "buy" rating on the stock.
Meantime analysts remained wary of a possible interest rate rise in UK next week as an incoming government aims to dampen the pace of growth and prevent a buildup in inflation pressures.

Economists said markets would also wait to see further U.S. economic reports such as Friday's U.S. employment report for evidence of the likely scale and timing of an expected U.S. interest rate increase. The U.S. Federal Reserve's decision-making committee next meets on May 20.

Cadbury fell 11p to 512-1/2 after the company announced disappointing first quarter soft drink sales figures in the U.S., while some utility stocks also came under pressure as investors turned cautious ahead of the election and a promised windfall tax on profits if Labour comes to power.
Thames Water fell 5-1/2p to 677p and Anglian Water dropped 10p to 670, yet Northern Ireland Electricity added 3-1/2p to 400-1/2 after analysts at BZW upgraded the stock to a "buy."
APV was up 16-1/2p at 87-1/2 after revealing shortly before yesterday's close a possible bid approach.
-- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4367
